statement: The jump amplitude of Paper B's meander prefactor is closed form: a_1 = 1/(2 theta sqrt(2 pi beta (1-beta))) = kappa theta* log3 / (2 theta) = 0.427956804, and a_0 = 2 theta a_1 = 1/sqrt(2 pi beta (1-beta)) = 0.826732564. WHY. psihat_k = Phihat_k * G(e(-k beta)) for every k, where Phi is the ladder profile of J-paper-b-ladder-profile-is-closed-form -- the k = 0 case is the mean, psihat_0 = kappa G(1), since Phihat_0 = kappa. Both sides carry a 1/k tail whose coefficient is a jump, so psi's jump at the origin is Phi's outright and a_1 is that over 2 theta. Measured mode by mode on psi at depth 1e6, |psihat_k| / |Phihat_k G_k| is 1.0015 +/- 0.0020 over k <= 256 with no trend against log k. Independently the free-amplitude level fit, extrapolated in 1/sqrt(N), gives 0.428027. THIS WITHDRAWS TWO VALUES RECORDED THE SAME DAY, 0.426227 and 0.426289, both about 0.4 percent low, for two different reasons that are worth keeping. The level-fit reading is low because a window of half-width delta around a jump contains every neighbouring jump, and those sum to about 17 sqrt(delta) -- so a local reading is low by O(1/sqrt(N)) and the level count has to be extrapolated rather than read. The sequence was visibly still climbing, 0.425355, 0.425679, 0.426217, 0.427025, 0.428359 at N = 2500 to 40000, and the earlier reading took a term for a limit. The Fourier reading is low because a complex least squares was fitted through a phase discrepancy of 0.085/k, and cos(0.085) = 0.9964 turns that phase into a magnitude deficit of almost exactly the 0.4 percent involved; the magnitudes alone always agreed. CONSEQUENCE. No fitted constant remains anywhere in psi: psihat_k = Phihat_k G(e(-k beta)) with Phihat closed form and G the Spitzer series in the exact counts. G(1) itself is still a convergent series and not an elementary closed form, so the meander constant kappa G(1) remains numerical -- but it is now numerical in one series rather than in a measured function.

The self-referential relation does not determine the jump amplitude. An earlier reading of this cluster proposed that a_n = A*psi(frac(n*beta))*n^(-3/2) together with periodicity is a fixed-point equation for psi in which A is scale-invariant, hence determined by the equation rather than by measurement. It is not. Written out, the relation is psi = C*1 + A*L psi, where L psi at x is sum_n psi(x_n) n^(-3/2) (x - 1{x_n <= x}), which is AFFINE in psi and not an eigenvalue problem: for every A it has the solution C*(I - A*L)^(-1)[1], a one-parameter family in C. Solved numerically on a four-thousand-point grid with four hundred modelled jumps, a solution exists at A = 0.2, 0.5, 0.82, 1.5, 3 and 8 alike, with I - A*L well conditioned throughout (condition number 3.3 to 384). The equation selects nothing. The obstruction behind it is sharper and is recorded with J-paper-b-psi-fourier-is-the-orbit-series: of all the Fourier coefficients of psi exactly one is in closed form independently of a_1, the mean kappa*G(1), and every other is proportional to a_1, so the one coefficient that could have closed the loop is the one a_1 does not appear in. Kind: the route is shut, and the question was then answered elsewhere. A closed form for a_1 is equivalent to a closed form for psi outright, and BOTH now exist -- not by bootstrapping psi against itself, which is what fails here, but by matching psi's Fourier tail against the ladder profile behind the Spitzer identity (J-paper-b-jump-amplitude-is-closed-form). The refutation of the fixed point stands; only its closing pessimism was wrong.

The jumps of Paper B's meander prefactor are the survivor sequence itself. Write N_d for the count of length-d parity words no prefix of which contracts, theta = beta^(-beta)(1-beta)^(beta-1)/2 for its exponential rate, and psi for the measured prefactor of J-paper-b-meander-prefactor-is-almost-periodic, a function of frac(d*beta) with beta = log2/log3. Then psi is discontinuous exactly on the rotation orbit, and its jump at frac(n*beta), left limit minus right limit, is a_n = a_1 * N_n / (2*theta)^(n-1) for every n >= 1; the jump at x = 0 is a_0 = 2*theta*a_1. There is exactly one constant in the statement, a_1, the amplitude at frac(beta), and it is CLOSED FORM: a_1 = 1/(2 theta sqrt(2 pi beta (1-beta))) = 0.427956804 (J-paper-b-jump-amplitude-is-closed-form). Values of 0.42623 and 0.426289 were recorded here earlier the same day as measurements and are withdrawn; both were about 0.4 percent low, and why is recorded with the closed form. Every other quantity is an exact integer over a power. WHY. psi(x) depends on x only through the barrier word read backwards from x, and crossing one point of the orbit transposes two adjacent letters, odd-then-even becoming even-then-odd, leaving the odd count and hence the barrier unchanged. The two histories differ by exactly the survivors standing on the barrier at the moment of the swap -- a single point mass -- which an odd letter fixes, so the difference is the survivor problem run again from one walker. That finite step is Lean-verified in PaperBJumpTransposition; the asymptotics that turn it into a statement about psi are measured, not proved. VERIFIED TWICE. A transfer-operator propagation using no measured data reproduces the identity to 2.3e-14 over n <= 3000. Independently, a one-parameter model of psi on d in [2e5,1e6] -- its jumps plus the linear rise periodicity demands -- gives a_1 = 0.42629, stable to 5e-4 across d-subranges, to 1e-4 as the number of modelled jumps runs from 1e4 to 1e6, and to between 0.03 and 0.35 percent against a freely fitted head amplitude for splits of the spectrum at n >= 5; the tightest split, a head of three jumps, reads 1.4 percent high. CONSEQUENCES. psi is of bounded variation. a_n is asymptotically 2*theta*a_1*psi(frac(n*beta))*n^(-3/2), so the jump of psi at the n-th orbit point is psi at that same point to a universal constant and a power. The barrier-index constants C_j = 2*a_1*theta^(1-j)*N_n/2^n, for any n with ceil(n*beta) = j, are now available at every j; the previous branch reached about j = 25 and no fit reaches further, because the column a fine jump contributes to any design collapses toward zero. WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. The jumps are not the function: jumps plus the linear rise leave a residual of 1.35e-02 against a level-fit noise floor of 4.4e-03, 89 percent of whose variance is a reproducible function of the coordinate and which does not shrink with d.

The jump spectrum of the meander prefactor and the series G(1) are the same object. Summing a_n = a_1 * N_n / (2*theta)^(n-1) over n >= 1 gives sum a_n = 2*theta*a_1*(G(1) - 1), where G(1) = sum over d >= 0 of N_d/(2*theta)^d is the one factor of the meander constant that J-paper-b-meander-constant-derived leaves numerical, about 7.07, against closed forms for kappa, sigma^2 and theta. Including the jump at x = 0 gives 2*theta*a_1*G(1), which is exactly the total continuous rise that periodicity of psi on the circle demands, and that constraint is met to 1.0 percent by the independent fit. So the summability of the jump spectrum -- the statement that psi is of bounded variation -- is the convergence of G(1), and a closed form for either is a closed form for the other. The numbers: at depth 1e6 the truncated G(1) is 7.0431 with a tail of about 0.022, the sum of downward jumps is 4.98, and the measured range of psi is 0.829 against a largest jump a_0 of 0.823.

The non-lattice local limit theorem constant is the mean of an explicit profile, and that profile is what generates psi. The Spitzer identity behind J-paper-b-meander-constant-derived exponentiates A_n = P(S_n >= 0)/theta^n, and that row invokes the non-lattice local limit theorem for A_n ~ kappa/sqrt(n), kappa = 1/(sqrt(2 pi) theta* sigma) = 1.541814521. That is true of the MEAN and of nothing else. Measured, A_n*sqrt(n) is a function of frac(n*beta) to 100 percent of its variance -- residual sd 0.0033 against a total sd of 0.238, and the two halves of the n-range agree to 0.00034 -- oscillating by about 15 percent around kappa. THE PROFILE IS CLOSED FORM. Since ceil(n*beta) - n*beta is exactly 1 - frac(n*beta), and consecutive binomial terms at the large-deviation point n*beta have ratio r = (1-beta)/beta, the tail is geometric to O(1/n) and Phi(x) = r^(1-x) / ((1-r) sqrt(2 pi beta (1-beta))). Checked pointwise without binning: the relative error is a pure 1/n offset, -7.8e-3, -1.9e-3, -8.1e-4 at n about 2000, 8000, 18000, with scatter falling 2.7e-3 to 1.5e-4. It is an exponential, not the sawtooth it first resembles; Phi(0.5) sits below the chord. TWO CONSEQUENCES IN CLOSED FORM. Its mean is 1/(log(beta/(1-beta)) sqrt(2 pi beta (1-beta))), which IS kappa identically -- beta/(1-beta) = log2/log(3/2), so log(beta/(1-beta)) = theta* log 3 and sqrt(2 pi beta (1-beta)) = sqrt(2 pi) sigma / log 3 -- agreeing to 2.2e-10. And its jump at the origin is one binomial term at the large-deviation point, rescaled: 1/sqrt(2 pi beta (1-beta)) = kappa theta* log 3 = 0.826732564. That jump is what fixes psi's amplitude (J-paper-b-jump-amplitude-is-closed-form). WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. Nothing here is proved: Phi is a measured profile with a derived closed form, the O(1/n) correction is not computed, and the local limit theorem it refines is quoted rather than re-derived.

The Fourier coefficients of Paper B's meander prefactor are the Wiener-Hopf series on the rotation orbit. The first step is not new and is already recorded in this cluster, in the test test_psi_is_reconstructed_from_its_jumps_and_that_settles_the_bv_tension: because psi jumps by a_n at frac(n*beta) and rises linearly in between by exactly the amount periodicity on the circle demands, as a distribution psi' = S - sum_n a_n delta_(x_n), so for k not 0 the k-th coefficient is psihat_k = -(1/(2*pi*i*k)) sum_n a_n e(-k*n*beta). That earlier reading left the sum opaque, measured only its growth (|S| about k^0.055) and did not identify it. WHAT IS NEW is that substituting the closed form of J-paper-b-jump-spectrum-is-the-survivor-sequence identifies it outright: psihat_k = -(2*theta*a_1/(2*pi*i*k)) * G(e(-k*beta)), where G(w) = sum_d N_d/(2*theta)^d w^d is the very series whose value at w = 1 is the numerical factor of J-paper-b-meander-constant-derived. So psi is determined in closed form up to the single constant a_1, and the gap that row records -- that G(1) stays numerical because a closed form for it needs psi, which nobody has -- is closed from the other side. VERIFIED. Coefficients measured independently by integrating a twenty-thousand-level fit of psi at depth 1e6 against e(-k x): |psihat_k| reads 9.940e-2, 5.977e-2, 5.600e-2, 2.824e-2, 4.552e-3 at k = 1, 2, 3, 5, 20 against 9.940e-2, 5.961e-2, 5.581e-2, 2.814e-2, 4.535e-3 predicted, phases agreeing to 0.085/k, and a complex least squares over k <= 60 recovering the amplitude to 2e-6 with a per-mode residual of 1.2 percent. A BETTER INSTRUMENT FOR a_1. The fit never has to separate one jump from its neighbours, so it is insensitive to the level count entirely -- 5000, 20000 and 40000 levels agree to six digits -- and gives a_1 = 0.426227 with a spread of 0.426096 to 0.426358 across d-subranges, against 0.426289 from the jump side. The two routes agree to 1.5e-4 and the recorded band tightens from 1.5e-3 to 2e-4. WHAT THIS DOES DETERMINE, CORRECTED THE SAME DAY. An earlier reading here concluded that a_1 is a constant of the problem rather than a consequence of its shape, on the grounds that the only coefficient in closed form without a_1 is the mean psihat_0 = kappa G(1). That was right about the mean and wrong about the conclusion: psihat_k = Phihat_k G(e(-k beta)) holds for EVERY k including zero, with Phi the ladder profile, so the 1/k tails on both sides match and a_1 follows from Phi's jump (J-paper-b-jump-amplitude-is-closed-form). The mean was not the only closed-form coefficient; all of them are. WHAT IS STILL UNEXPLAINED, AND A CORRECTION. The part of psi the jump spectrum misses has a Fourier spectrum decaying like k^(-1.74), faster than psi's own k^(-1), so it is not another jump family; past k about 30 the measured residual flattens near 0.4 percent, which is the level fit's floor rather than structure, so no exponent is claimed. This supersedes the reading in test_psi_is_reconstructed_from_its_jumps_and_that_settles_the_bv_tension, which found that residual spectrum FLAT (0.00175 low-n against 0.00134 high-n) and concluded it was the unresolved tail of small jumps on a dense orbit. That test measured its amplitudes by local differencing, which is biased low by 3.5 percent at n = 1 rising to 31 percent by n = 12; a uniformly under-subtracted jump family leaves a jump-like remainder and a jump-like remainder has a flat spectrum. The flatness was the bias, not the residual.

The 1/rho law for the jump amplitudes is the empty-window theorem, and carries nothing else. This cluster recorded that the ratio of consecutive jump amplitudes across a Sturmian zero -- an n with ceil(n*beta) = ceil((n-1)*beta) -- is exactly 1/rho = 1.0352968376, measured first to 7.6e-4 by a level fit and then to 2.1e-12 by a deterministic propagation. The law is exact and it is trivial. First, rho and theta are the same number, 0.96590655323343772361, under two names [CORRECTED 2026-09-20: this row recorded 0.9659065532355213, wrong from the twelfth significant digit, 2.08e-12 above the true value. The laboratory CODE was never wrong -- paper_b_prefix_count.chernoff_rate() returns 0.9659065532334377 and plain double precision gives 0.9659065532334378, so this was a transcription into prose and not a computation. The provenance of the wrong digits is unknown: they are not the double-precision value and not 1/(1.0352968376), which gives 0.9659065532530513. The quoted 1/rho = 1.0352968376 is a correct rounding of 1.0352968376210226 and stands. Note the row also quotes an agreement of 2.1e-12 for this law, the same magnitude as the error just removed; the two are not known to be related and the agreement was not re-derived here], which is what made the ratio look like an independent constant. Second, a Sturmian zero is an even barrier letter, an even letter kills nothing and doubles the survivor count exactly, and dividing by the normalisation 2*theta leaves 1/theta. The doubling is the statement of PaperBCertificateLengths that no minimal certificate exists at a length where no power of three lies in the window, seen from the amplitude side, and it is one line in Lean (PaperBJumpTransposition.total_stepFlat_eq_two_mul). The reading is retracted as a finding and kept as an identity. What survives is the direction it pointed: the content of the spectrum is entirely in the odd letters, which is what led to the closed form of J-paper-b-jump-spectrum-is-the-survivor-sequence.

Paper B's survivor count is OEIS A076227, a known Collatz quantity, and this cluster's earlier reading of the literature as independent was wrong. The counts N_d of length-d parity words no prefix of which contracts agree with the b-file of Hikawa and Nakanishi on all 3509 terms, n = 0 to 3508, the last of which has 999 digits -- an independent check far past the nine enumerated terms the laboratory had been using. The sequence entered OEIS through Labos Elemer in October 2002 under a Collatz reading: the number of residue classes modulo 2^n in which the stopping time A074473 is not constant. A comment of Kazunobu Hikawa, 21 July 2026, states the laboratory's own definition outright -- the binary words v(1)..v(n) with 2^m < 3^(v(1)+...+v(m)) for every m -- and the entry carries a dynamic program equivalent to the height program used here. WHAT THE IDENTIFICATION BUYS. The asymptotic of this cluster becomes a statement about a Collatz quantity: the share of residue classes modulo 2^n whose stopping time is undetermined is psi(frac(n beta)) theta^n n^(-3/2), where the OEIS entry itself records only that the share tends to zero, bounded by 2114/65536 or about 3.23 percent at n = 16. It also supplies 3509 exact terms against which any future change to the counting program can be checked. PRIORITY SETTLED BY READING THE SOURCES, 19 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND TWO OF THE FOUR PIECES ARE PRIOR WORK. (1) THE EXPONENTIAL RATE IS LAGARIAS 1985, THEOREM D, AND IS THIS LABORATORY'S THETA TO THIRTY DIGITS. In the survey's notation, for all k >= 1, (2.17) 1 - F(k) = lim_x (1/x) #{n <= x : sigma(n) > k} <= 2^(-eta k) with (2.18) eta = 1 - H(theta_L) about .05004, H the binary entropy function and theta_L = (log_2 3)^(-1) = beta. The proof sets C_2 = {v inflating, length k}, notes 2^(-k)|C_2| = 1 - F(k) -- so |C_2| IS N_k -- and bounds it by the binomial tail sum over j > k theta_L of C(k,j) through Ash Lemma 4.7.2; the remark that follows gives the matching lower bound 1 - F(k) >= 2^(-(eta+epsilon)k) for every epsilon > 0 and all large k, so the estimate is two-sided on the exponential scale. Numerically eta = 0.050044472811669365186 and 2^(-eta) = 0.9659065532334377236055 = beta^(-beta) (1-beta)^(beta-1) / 2, agreeing to all thirty digits computed. The Lean bound neverNegCount_div_pow_le_theta of PaperBSurvivorDecay (J-survivor-count-decay) is therefore Theorem D's upper half, and Kontorovich-Lagarias 2009 quote the same thing as O(2^(0.94995k)) out of 2^k, 0.94995 being H(beta) = log_2(2 theta). Theorem D carries no attribution label in the survey, unlike its Theorems A and C which are labelled (Terras); Lagarias's own annotated bibliography credits Terras 1976 with the residue-class structure, the coefficient stopping time and natural density one, and not with a rate. Terras 1976 itself could not be read -- the matwbn scan sits behind an anti-bot gate -- so this attribution rests on Lagarias. (2) THE d^(-3/2) WAS CONJECTURED BEFORE THIS CLUSTER MEASURED IT. Hikawa, July 2026, Conjecture 7.1: W(d) = Theta(d^(-3/2) 2^(gamma d)), motivated by the residual log_2 W(d) - gamma d agreeing with the ballot-type correction -(3/2) log_2 d to within 0.3 bits over 100 <= d <= 10000. The same paper proves in Section 6 the logarithmic asymptotic log_2 W(d) = gamma d + O(log d) with gamma = lambda H(1/lambda) about 1.5056, lambda = log_2 3, and decay rate c = lambda(1 - H(1/lambda)) about 0.0793 bits per unit weight, by a cycle lemma plus entropy estimates, with a length-basis analogue. That is the weight basis: gamma = H(beta)/beta = 1.5056438879463007943 and c = eta/beta = 0.079318612774855387135, so Hikawa's constants are Lagarias's eta rescaled by 1/beta and Section 6 is an independent proof of the same rate. The O(log d) there cannot see the -3/2, which is why the -3/2 is a separate conjecture. Conjecture 7.1 is a Theta and not an asymptotic equivalence, it is not proved, and its 0.3-bit tolerance is wide enough to absorb this cluster's psi, whose range 10.37..11.21 is 0.11 bits. (3) THE OSCILLATION AND (4) a_1 WERE NOT FOUND ANYWHERE. No source read states an oscillating or almost-periodic prefactor in frac(d beta), an amplitude, or anything equivalent to the jump spectrum: Lagarias 1985 and his annotated bibliography, Kontorovich-Lagarias 2009, Winkler 2017-2026 v8 in full plus his September 2026 Beatty-Ferrers preprint, Hikawa July and September 2026, Hikawa-Nakanishi January 2026, Nakanishi February 2026 in full, Rozier-Terracol v5 in full, and Niu v1. QUALIFIED THE SAME DAY, AND IT IS THE NEAREST MISS: reading A076227 alone misses that the orbit structure is in the literature on the companion sequence. A comment of Winkler on A100982 dated 15 September 2026, four days before this reading and verified here against the entry, gives (1/n) C(m_n - 1, n - 1) <= a(n) <= (1/n) C(m_n, n - 1) with m_n = floor(n log_2 3), equality in the lower bound exactly at strict record minima of {n log_2 3} and in the upper bound exactly at strict record maxima, the equality orders being the one-sided convergents and semiconvergents of log_2 3 and a(n) a rational Catalan number there. A100982 is this laboratory's M_d, so those are the same words on the same coordinate, and the Sturmian half of this cluster has published company. The bounds are a factor about 2.7 apart, so they carry no polynomial correction and no prefactor and neither give nor contradict the d^(-3/2) or psi; checked on the laboratory's counts to order 2213 by a peer session (J-winkler-sandwich-holds-on-the-laboratory-counts). What remains unrecorded is an ASYMPTOTIC prefactor, not the fact that these counts are organised by the rotation orbit. WHAT COULD NOT BE READ, WHICH BOUNDS THE CLAIM. Hikawa July 2026 and Hikawa-Nakanishi January 2026 are ResearchGate-gated: the record and the author-written version note were read in the browser pane, the bodies were not. Terras 1976 and Everett 1977 were not read directly. So (3) and (4) are statements about what was readable, not about what exists. CONSEQUENCE FOR HOW THIS CLUSTER IS WRITTEN. The asymptotic is a refinement of Theorem D and of Conjecture 7.1, not a discovery: the rate is Lagarias's, the exponent is Hikawa's, and what is added here is the prefactor -- that it exists, that it oscillates on the rotation orbit, and that it is computable (J-paper-b-meander-prefactor-is-almost-periodic, J-paper-b-jump-spectrum-is-the-survivor-sequence, J-paper-b-jump-amplitude-is-closed-form, J-paper-b-psi-fourier-is-the-orbit-series). Novelty language on the rate or on the exponent is withdrawn. Literature ids: oeis-A076227, lagarias-1985-3x+1-problem, terras-1976-stopping-time, everett-1977-iteration, winkler-2017-2026-deterministic-structures, hikawa-2026-parity-vector-structures, hikawa-nakanishi-2026-parity-vector-analysis, nakanishi-2026-parity-vector-structure, rozier-terracol-2026, oeis-A100982, kontorovich-lagarias-2009-stochastic-models, niu-2026-parity-vectors-paradoxical. CARRIED BY PAPER B, 2026-09-19: the manuscript's Section 1 now states the identity outright (same two-step walk on log x and on log log n, so a word contracts in one problem exactly when it contracts in the other), names A076227 for the survivor counts with its 2002 OEIS reading, A100982 (Finch, admissible sequences) for the minimal certificates and A020914 for their admissible lengths, disclaims priority for all three, and says where the two problems part: for Collatz the word of length d is a function of x mod 2^d and the fair-share densities are free by Terras, while for Juggler they are Hypothesis FD, which is the analytic burden of the paper. Lemma 5.1 is labelled as verifying the first terms of A100982 rather than establishing them; Remark 6.2 says the decay it proves is a statement about Collatz residue classes as well; the Section 8 evidence table carries a row 'Word counts, certificate lengths, and the survivor decay | Shared with the Collatz literature ... no priority claimed'; references 5 to 7 are the three OEIS entries. The unconditional analytic theorems 3.1, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 are unaffected: they count starting values by nested floor powers and have no Collatz counterpart.

Transposing two adjacent barrier letters costs exactly the mass on the barrier. Grade the surviving parity words of a given length by their surplus h above the barrier. A barrier letter that does not rise acts by stepFlat v h = v h + v (h-1) and kills nothing; one that rises acts by stepRise v h = v (h+1) + v h and loses exactly v 0, the survivors sitting on the barrier. Then stepRise (stepFlat v) and stepFlat (stepRise v) agree at every height except zero and differ at zero by exactly v 0 (stepRise_stepFlat_eq_add_barrierMass). Since every later letter acts linearly (run_add), the whole difference between the two transposed histories is the history of a single point mass at the barrier (run_stepRise_stepFlat), and an odd letter fixes that point mass (stepRise_barrierMass). At the level of totals, a flat letter doubles below a window the profile has not reached (total_stepFlat_eq_two_mul) and a rising letter doubles less the barrier mass (total_stepRise_add_barrierMass). Everything is over the natural numbers; no real number appears in any statement, and the two orders are comparable with one dominating the other (run_stepFlat_stepRise_le). This is the finite core under J-paper-b-jump-spectrum-is-the-survivor-sequence: it is why a discontinuity of the meander prefactor is not a new quantity but the survivor problem restarted from one walker. It does not say that the prefactor exists, that the d^(-3/2) is right, or that the propagated difference converges to the jump.
